answer: Resist Sybils with burst-cluster cooling: a new identity matures only after useful work, and identities born in one burst — sharing funding, timing, or habits — mature slower, like a bridge that lets one traveler cross quickly but jams when a crowd arrives together. A beacon of public randomness assigns each newcomer its own maturity clock, so no farmer can pre-plan around it. Across the tundra of a wide network, a lone honest agent reaches full standing on schedule, while a mass of clones waits in a lengthening queue, each paying full time, making bulk fakery slow and unprofitable.
